findings.message: Gas piping, regulators, safety valves and the installation must be done or checked by a licensed gas fitter to your local code (NFPA 54 and 58 in the US).
The front wall is the door: bricked up, dry, for each firing. Lay the inner and outer courses together, staggered, with a header course two-thirds of the way up.
Side-mounted burners need a bag wall so the flames don't hit the ware: hard brick, first course solid in front of the burners.
Damper: a kiln shelf in a slot 7.5 in wide and one course high, about a foot above the top of the flue. Brace the chimney with angle at its corners and tie it to the kiln frame.

Three spy holes, 2¼ × 2½ in (a quarter brick), in the door: about 8 in above the floor (a course above any burner ports there), midway and near the top, a few inches off centre so they miss the shelf posts. Cone packs in the top and bottom, draw rings in the middle.

Arch bricks: Back wall, layer 1 from the inside: about 63 bricks by volume, cut to the curve; Back wall, layer 2 from the inside: about 63 bricks by volume, cut to the curve; Door, layer 1 from the inside: about 63 bricks by volume, cut to the curve; Door, layer 2 from the inside: about 63 bricks by volume, cut to the curve; Catenary arch, layer 1 from the inside: about 281 bricks by volume, cut to the curve.
